comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C3, C95 regarding gene structure and evolutionary conservation. Both evaluations find these foundational characterization claims well-supported by phylogenetic and genomic data.

Both support testis-specific expression claims C4-C7. OpenEval also includes C115 (stage-specific expression switch), which peer reviewers address separately in R16. Both find expression data convincing.

Both support structural predictions (C8-C9) and Golgi localization (C10-C11). OpenEval notes homodimer claim remains somewhat speculative without direct biochemical validation, while peer reviewers accept without specific concern.
Both support Golgi localization claims C10-C11, C20. OpenEval focuses on immunostaining colocalization with GM130, while peer reviewers accept as part of thorough characterization.

Strong agreement on knockout validation claims C12-C14, C16-C17, C20. OpenEval emphasizes molecular characterization details, peer reviewers note mutant phenotype is strong and interesting with supported conclusions.

Perfect agreement on male sterility phenotype claims C22-C25. Both find the complete sterility with normal spermatogenesis well-supported by comprehensive phenotypic characterization and statistical analyses.
Partial overlap on knockout phenotype. OpenEval R6 covers broader phenotypic characterization including sterility, while peer R4 focuses on knockout generation and validation aspects (C15, C21).
Perfect agreement on sperm head morphology claims C26-C31. Both accept the quantitative morphological analysis and conclusion that additional factors beyond head shape contribute to sterility.

Perfect agreement on IVF defects claims C32-C39. Both find the ZP binding and fusion defects well-supported with appropriate statistics, and accept the dose-response rescue demonstrating partial overcome of defects.
Perfect agreement on UTJ migration defects claims C40-C42. Both accept the fluorescence microscopy evidence showing knockout sperm fail to reach the oviduct as convincing.

Both support glycosylation defect claims, with partial overlap. OpenEval R10 focuses on C43-C48 (ZPBP1, SPACA1 glycosylation), while peer R9 covers broader protein processing including these and additional claims C49-C60.

Strong agreement on abnormal protein processing claims C49-C57. OpenEval emphasizes ADAM3 processing defects are glycosylation-dependent, peer reviewers accept as part of comprehensive abnormal processing findings.

Both support LYPD4 processing defects claims C58-C60. OpenEval notes inference about processing errors is reasonable but requires further characterization, peer reviewers accept as part of abnormal glycosylation.
Perfect agreement on IZUMO1 claims C61-C63. Both accept reduced levels with proper relocalization as supported by western blot and immunofluorescence data.
Perfect agreement on glycosylation defects claims C64-C70. Both accept the discrepancy between mass spec and western blot as evidence for glycosylation defects rather than protein absence.
Both support SPACA6 findings (C72). OpenEval emphasizes mechanistic distinction from other knockout models, peer reviewers accept as part of glycosylation analysis.
Strong agreement on lectin blot analysis claims C73-C78. Both accept the comprehensive lectin analysis demonstrating disrupted galactose modifications and differential effects on glycan structures.
Perfect agreement on UDP-GlcNAc transporter function claims C79-C82. Both find the rescue experiments in SLC35B4 knockout cells convincing evidence for transporter activity.
Both support human variant claims C83-C87. OpenEval notes clinical significance remains to be determined, while peer reviewers accept variants as implicating human infertility based on mouse data.

Both support functional validation of human variants claims C88-C90. OpenEval notes experiments in heterologous system, peer reviewers accept as demonstrating impaired transporter activity relevant to human infertility.
Perfect agreement on main conclusions claims C91-C92, C96-C98, C141-C142. Both find the comprehensive evidence supports SLC35G3 as essential for male fertility with likely human conservation.

Divergence on human fertility implications claims C93-C94, C143-C144. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting lack of human patient data and speculative extrapolation, while peer reviewers SUPPORT based on mouse data and variant analysis.

Both address human relevance claims C143-C144. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN requiring clinical validation, peer reviewers SUPPORT stating human conservation is likely and variants implicate infertility.

Perfect agreement on glycan elongation mechanism claims C122-C125. Both accept the distinction between core structure and elongation based on lectin blot patterns showing normal mannose but altered elongated structures.
Perfect agreement on multiple functional defects claims C126, C129. Both accept normal histology with functional defects in ZPBP1 and SPACA1 as well-documented.
Both support ADAM3 presence claims C131-C132. OpenEval notes speculation about dysfunction requires further investigation, peer reviewers accept as distinguishing feature from other models.

OpenEval addresses selective pressure claims C137-C138 based on gnomAD analysis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these population genetics inferences are not explicitly discussed by reviewers.

Both support IVF rescue and clinical implications claims C139-C140. OpenEval notes human application is speculative requiring validation, peer reviewers accept clinical implication as logical from experimental results.

Both address stage-specific expression switch claims C115-C121. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN noting authors acknowledge speculation and unclear functional differences, peer reviewers SUPPORT as part of accepted expression characterization.
OpenEval addresses species differences and research priorities claims C133-C134. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these comparative biology recommendations are not explicitly discussed.
OpenEval addresses future applications claim C145. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this speculative statement about potential applications is not explicitly evaluated by reviewers.
